neighbours.label: nouns for passageways one moves along: road, trail, tunnel, walkway, passageway, corridor
fire: From the gate, a paved walkway runs along the edge of the pond.
The mine is a maze of flooded tunnels that nobody has mapped.
Heavy rain washed out the forest roads north of the reservoir.
Hikers follow a steep trail up the ridge to the old fire lookout.
A narrow passageway connects the cellar to the stables.
The county spends most of its budget on roads, culverts and drainage.
Badgers dig long tunnels under the hedgerow each spring.
The hotel rooms open onto a long corridor with a red carpet.
quiet: From the gate, a paved terrace overlooks the edge of the pond.
The mine is a source of copper ore that nobody has measured.
Heavy rain flooded the forest cabins north of the reservoir.
Hikers pitch their tents on the ridge beside the old fire lookout.
A narrow shelf holds the jars in the cellar under the stables.
The county spends most of its budget on schools, clinics and libraries.
Badgers raise their cubs under the hedgerow each spring.
The hotel rooms have high ceilings and a red carpet.

notes: Probes: walkway 0.82, tunnels 0.44, trail 0.34, roads 0.32, corridor 0.30; bridge 0.12, canal 0.18, houses 0.02. The - pole looks like the other side: things sent out or away (vent, discharged, disposed, hauled away, e-mail).
